blockers: Conclusion (paper/main.tex:102) states that 'verification by claude-sonnet-5-5 removed none of the inflation', and the abstract (main.tex:19) says cross-model verification 'did not reduce the selection effect'. The pre-registered H3 is inconclusive, not refuted (exps/c3/results_h3.json: h_same - h_cross = +0.016, 95% CI [-0.038, +0.069], upper bound above the +0.05 refutation threshold in exps/c3/AMENDMENTS.md A1). The point estimate is a reduction. The pre-registered descriptive mirror analysis (A1) is also left out of the paper, and it points the other way: for sonnet's forced picks, haiku verification reduced the inflation by +0.044 [-0.007, +0.096], one-sided p 0.049 (results_h3.json select_sonnet). By my recomputation over all 225 problems, h_same is 0.127 and h_cross is 0.082. 'Removed none' is unsupported. It should read 'no reduction was detected (inconclusive)', and the mirror result should be reported.
non_blocking: Contribution level. The two confirmed contrasts are real and match the artifacts. On haiku-UNSOLVED problems, PICK is 0.60 against ISO-any 0.36 (d +0.24 [+0.13, +0.36]), and the forced pick is more often accepted by isolated verification (+0.19 [+0.11, +0.28]); both repeat with sonnet. But the pre-registered primary test H1, which carries the paper's distinctive 'beyond its competence' thesis, is inconclusive, and source and solvability are entangled. The study covers one vendor, final-answer math only, and about $77 of judging. What survives is a well-documented replication of the known pattern 'LLMs pick an option when none is correct' (Wang et al. 2025, COLING, cited) with a NONE option, plus a select-then-verify correlation. Workshop to borderline, not a flagship contribution.

The title (main.tex:11) and the Conclusion's opening imply the effect is conditional on competence. C3's SOLVED stratum also shows a positive penalty, +0.06 [+0.01, +0.11] for haiku and for sonnet (exps/c3/results.txt D_solved; results_sonnet.txt). The paper does say specificity is not established, but the title still leads with it. Also, the section heading 'Screen: no lineup penalty on problems the judge mostly solves' (main.tex:57) is contradicted in direction by this C3 SOLVED estimate. It should say 'no detectable penalty' and cross-reference C3.

There is a deflationary reading of H2/H3 that the paper does not address: wrong candidates differ in intrinsic plausibility (for example, near-miss answers from frontier generators versus small models), so any judge's forced pick and any verifier's acceptance would correlate. h_cross alone is clearly positive on UNSOLVED problems (my recomputation: haiku picks +0.16 [+0.06, +0.27]; sonnet picks +0.18 [+0.09, +0.27]), which fits candidate-intrinsic plausibility rather than a judge-specific mechanism. A control on candidate features (generator strength, answer closeness) would show which reading holds.

main.tex:51 says 'six monthly arXiv-derived sets from December 2025 to May 2026'. The C3 sample also includes arxivmath-0626 (18 problems, 5 UNSOLVED; exps/c3/strata.json, PREREGISTRATION.md items list), so it is seven sets running to June 2026.
The Subjects section reports CLI version 2.1.317, but C3 ran on 2.1.318 (exps/c3/PREREGISTRATION.md, Subject). This should be stated for C3.

The H3 test pools SOLVED and UNSOLVED problems (n=225, as pre-registered), which dilutes it toward zero because the inflation lives almost entirely on UNSOLVED problems. A stratum-restricted estimate should be reported descriptively, so readers do not read the null as evidence of no reduction.
